title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. $\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}$ is the profinite completion of $PSL(2,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z/2 * \mathbb Z/3$, which Grothendieck writes as $Sl(2,\mathbb Z)^{\wedge\prime}$. It is generated by $\sigma_\infty$ (order 2) and $\rho$ (order 3), with $\varepsilon_0=\sigma_\infty\rho$. Its normal subgroup $\hat\Pi_{0,3}$ is the completion of $\Gamma(2)/\pm1$, i.e. the free profinite group on two generators, $\hat\pi_1(\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})$. The quotient is $\mathfrak S_3=PSL(2,\mathbb F_2)$.

The group studied. $\mathcal N^{!\sim}_{0,3}$ is the group of automorphisms $u$ of $\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}$ that stabilise $\hat\Pi_{0,3}$, act trivially on $\mathfrak S_3$, and preserve the 'loop structure', i.e. the conjugacy class of $\varepsilon_0$ up to $\hat{\mathbb Z}^*$-powers (inertia up to the cyclotomic multiplier). The previous page explains why: $\Gamma_{\mathbb Q}=\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q)$ embeds in this group. The programme is to compute the group explicitly, then cut it down by further necessary conditions towards a characterisation of $\Gamma_{\mathbb Q}$.

Parametrisation. Since $u$ acts trivially mod $\hat\Pi$, one may write $u(\sigma_\infty)=h\sigma_\infty$ and $u(\rho)=g\rho$ with $h,g\in\hat\Pi_{0,3}$. Such a pair defines an endomorphism exactly when the free-product relations survive: $(h\sigma_\infty)^2=(g\rho)^3=1$. Writing $\sigma_\infty(x)$, $\rho(x)$ for conjugation, these become $h\,\sigma_\infty(h)=1$ and $g\,\rho(g)\,\rho^2(g)=1$, eq. (25).

Loop condition. One requires $u(\varepsilon_0)=f^{-1}\varepsilon_0^{\mu}f$ with $f\in\hat\Pi_{0,3}$ and $\mu\in\hat{\mathbb Z}^*$. Here $f$ is determined modulo the centraliser $\hat\Pi\cap\overline{\langle\varepsilon_0\rangle}=\overline{\langle l_0\rangle}$, where $l_0=\varepsilon_0^2$. On the next page this is unwound, with $\nu=(\mu-1)/2$ (possible since $\mu$ is odd), into the boxed relation $\sigma_\infty(h)\,g=\sigma_\infty(f)^{-1}\,l_1^{\nu}\,\rho(f)$.

Modern reading. This is a three-unknown version of the description of $\widehat{GT}$-type elements $(\lambda,f)$:
- The order-2 relation is Drinfeld's 2-cycle relation (I).
- The order-3 relation plus the loop relation together encode the 3-cycle/hexagon relation (II).
- $\nu=(\mu-1)/2$ is exactly Drinfeld's $m=(\lambda-1)/2$.

No pentagon (M_{0,5}) condition appears yet. So $\mathcal N^{!\sim}_{0,3}$ corresponds to the 'genus-0, 3-point' part of $\widehat{GT}$: the group cut out by relations (I),(II) only, possibly up to the inner/centraliser ambiguity in $f$.
errors: No genuine error. Formulas (24)->(25) check out: (h s)^2 = h s h s^{-1} = h s(h), and (g r)^3 = g r(g) r^2(g) r^3. The identification of the normal subgroup and of the quotient S_3 is correct.
Formulas (23)-(25) only give an endomorphism; bijectivity is not automatic. Grothendieck flags this himself ('ou du moins un endomorphisme') and adds a 'condition liminaire' on the next page.
'Sl(2,Z)^' should be read as the completion of PSL(2,Z) (presumably what the prime indicates). The free product Z/2*Z/3 is PSL, not SL.

ideas.what: Embedding Gal(Qbar/Q) into automorphisms of the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) that preserve the congruence-2 subgroup (free profinite group F2), act trivially on S_3, and preserve inertia classes up to cyclotomic powers
ideas.modern_name: S_3-equivariant outer Galois action on pi_1(P^1-{0,1,infty}); GT-hat type group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi (faithfulness, 1979); Ihara (1980s); Drinfeld (1990); Ihara, Lochak-Schneps, Harbater-Schneps for profinite GT
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), conceptually; La Longue Marche (1981, circulated)

ideas.what: Parametrisation u(sigma_inf)=h sigma_inf, u(rho)=g rho with h sigma_inf(h)=1, g rho(g) rho^2(g)=1
ideas.modern_name: 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of GT-hat, here stated on PSL2(Z)^ = Z/2*Z/3
ideas.where_published: Possibly in Longue Marche drafts; not in Esquisse explicitly

ideas.what: Loop condition u(eps_0) = f^{-1} eps_0^mu f, with nu=(mu-1)/2 giving the boxed relation sigma_inf(h) g = sigma_inf(f)^{-1} l_1^nu rho(f)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly derives the 2-cycle relation, a 3-cycle relation, and the half-cyclotomic parameter nu=(mu-1)/2 for the group of loop-preserving automorphisms of PSL2(Z)^. This appears to predate Drinfeld's (1990) GT-hat relations, with exactly the same normalisation m=(lambda-1)/2. Usually only the conceptual anticipation (Esquisse) is credited, not explicit relations of this form.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the explicit genus-0, 3-point part of GT-hat. It also offers a three-parameter (h,g,f) presentation via PSL2(Z)^ that differs from the usual one-parameter f(x,y). That presentation may be useful for comparing GT-hat with automorphism groups of PSL2(Z)^ / B_3^ (Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura).

missed.claim: The stated programme: compute N^{!~}_{0,3} and accumulate necessary conditions on its elements until Gal(Q) is characterised (even only plausibly). This is the still-open question of whether GT-hat equals Gal(Qbar/Q).
missed.quote: trouver un maximum de conditions nécessaires sur des éléments de N^{!~}_{0,3} pour provenir de Γ_Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The GT-hat = Gal(Q) problem remains open; the subsequent pages may contain conditions not yet catalogued.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an explicit, correct derivation of GT-type relations (including the m=(λ-1)/2 normalisation) in Grothendieck's own S_3/PSL2(Z) language, likely dating from around 1981, before Drinfeld. Its existence is broadly known in spirit through the Esquisse and Longue Marche, so it is notable rather than shocking.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note under (22) should read roughly 'f déterminé mod f ↦ l_0^n f, n ∈ Ẑ' (centraliser of ε0 in Π̂ is generated by l0 = ε0²), not 'h^n f, n ∈ Z'.
Third line of (23) is struck out in the image.
(21): 'respectant la structure à lacets (définie par la classe de ε0)'; 'Sl(2,Z)^∧′' denotes the completed (P)SL(2,Z).
